content.question_text: What is the approach used with modern data structures regarding separating Collection interfaces and implementation?

core_requirements: Refer to the collection using an interface-type variable
Only call methods defined by that interface on the collection, not implementation-specific methods

content.question_text: What is NOT possible when following this interface-based approach?

core_requirements: You cannot call methods specific to the concrete implementation class (only the declared interface's methods)

content.question_text: In the Collection interface, what does the add() method return?

core_requirements: Returns true if adding the element actually changed the collection

content.question_text: Describe the methods of the Iterator interface.
Why can't you just repeatedly call next() alone on an Iterator without anything else?

core_requirements: Calling next() past the end of the iteration throws a NoSuchElementException

content.question_text: What needs to be called before calling next() to safely avoid an exception?
How does the for-each loop work under the hood, in terms of what types it can operate on?

core_requirements: It works with any object that implements the Iterable interface

content.question_text: What is a for-each loop actually translated to by the compiler?

core_requirements: A loop using an Iterator (calling hasNext()/next() internally)

content.question_text: What's an easier way to loop through a collection than manually using hasNext()/next()?

core_requirements: Call the forEach() method, passing a lambda that consumes each element
